analysis:
The supplied units are CHANGELOG.md head-text excerpts (lines 1064-1573). The PR adds a v0.10.7 candidate section and retains older release notes; no source code, config or workflow is changed in these units. I examined the notes against the threat model for statements that could signal an unrecorded security change or invalidate stated assumptions. Relevant areas:
- SSD prefix cache (T-041): v0.10.5 notes describe concurrent restores, a restore refreshing checkpoint mtime only while no other request holds the file, TTL maintenance consulting the loaded cache's last-restore record, a header cache for the maintenance walk, and chunked sweeps. They state TTL, budget and ownership decisions are unchanged. The 30-minute TTL and HMAC names are unaffected. The mtime-refresh and in-memory last-restore behavior is implementation detail I cannot verify from prose; it could subtly affect the TTL/sliding-window semantics but is described as preserving the bound, so no finding.
- Add-on hold (TB-012, T-059, T-060): the v0.10.4 hardening notes (signer check before slot use, 10 s request-line deadline, FIFO refusal, model-load fence) match the threat model's description.
- Sandbox CLI installer (TB-013, T-061): the v0.10.5 note says the installer is downloaded over HTTPS and run. This is already covered by T-061 and shows no new change here.
- Release and CI workflow notes (dev branch lane, source gate, designated-requirement check) concern the signed-artifact contract. They are prose only; the workflow files are not supplied, so the gate behavior is unverified.
- The TP/GLM/Qwen performance and media-handling notes describe unspecified implementation changes; sealed 256 KiB pieces remain authenticated per the notes. The v0.10.7 notes require both pair Macs to run the same build (fail-closed).
Remaining uncertainty: the underlying code changes (cluster wire, the sealed-piece encryption, the cache-sweep locking) are not in the supplied units and cannot be assessed. A final pass should examine those source files if they are in the PR.
